textbooks.title: Starter Listening Foundations
textbooks.description: Short, clear classroom sentences for first-pass dictation and confidence building.

questions.sentence: Students should review their notes before exams.

support.meaning: This sentence says students need to study their notes before a test.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the verb phrase "review their notes" and the final time phrase "before exams".

vocabulary.exams: tests that check what students have learned

questions.sentence: The teacher asked everyone to underline the main idea.

support.meaning: The teacher told the class to mark the most important point in the text.
support.listeningFocus: Catch the action chain "asked everyone to underline" and the final phrase "the main idea".

vocabulary.underline: to draw a line under a word or sentence

questions.sentence: Our class worked together to finish the science poster.

support.meaning: The class cooperated to complete a poster for science.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the teamwork phrase "worked together" and the object at the end, "science poster".

vocabulary.poster: a large sheet used to present information

textbooks.title: Academic Bridge Practice
textbooks.description: Academic sentences that train connectors, cause and effect, and higher-accuracy listening.

questions.sentence: Although he was tired, he finished the assignment.

support.meaning: Even though he felt tired, he still completed the work.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the contrast opener "Although" and the ending noun "assignment".

questions.sentence: Researchers often compare multiple sources before drawing a conclusion.

support.meaning: Researchers usually look at several sources before deciding what they think.
support.listeningFocus: Focus on the academic verbs "compare" and "drawing a conclusion".

questions.sentence: In contrast, the second experiment produced more reliable results.

support.meaning: This sentence shows a difference: the second experiment gave better and more dependable results.
support.listeningFocus: Catch the contrast signal "In contrast" and the adjective phrase "more reliable results".

vocabulary.in contrast: showing a difference from something else

questions.sentence: As a result, the new policy improved student participation in class.

support.meaning: Because of that change, the new policy made students join in more during class.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the cause-and-effect starter "As a result" and the phrase "student participation".

textbooks.title: Discussion and Response Builder
textbooks.description: Longer response-style prompts for debate, reading follow-up, and presentation practice.

questions.sentence: During the debate, each student supported an opinion with clear evidence.

support.meaning: In the debate, every student gave evidence to support an opinion.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the setting phrase "During the debate" and the academic phrase "clear evidence".

vocabulary.debate: a formal discussion with different opinions
vocabulary.evidence: facts or examples that support an idea

questions.sentence: After reading the article, the class discussed two possible solutions.

support.meaning: Once the class finished the article, they talked about two ways to solve the problem.
support.listeningFocus: Catch the time phrase "After reading the article" and the ending phrase "two possible solutions".

questions.sentence: The speaker explained the chart before answering questions from the audience.

support.meaning: The presenter described the chart first and then answered people's questions.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the sequence words "before answering" and the final noun "audience".

questions.sentence: By the end of the lesson, students could summarize the passage in their own words.

support.meaning: At the end of the lesson, students were able to explain the passage using their own language.
support.listeningFocus: Focus on the time opener "By the end of the lesson" and the verb phrase "summarize the passage".

vocabulary.summarize: to give the main points briefly

textbooks.title: TOEFL Test Textbook
textbooks.description: Lecture-style and academic listening sentences designed for TOEFL-style note-taking and response accuracy.

questions.sentence: The professor argued that migration patterns shift when food sources become less predictable.

support.meaning: The professor said animals or people may move differently when food is harder to predict.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the reporting verb "argued" and the cause phrase "when food sources become less predictable".

vocabulary.migration patterns: the usual ways people or animals move from one place to another
vocabulary.predictable: able to be expected in advance

questions.sentence: According to the lecture, urban planners must balance economic growth with environmental protection.

support.meaning: The lecture says city planners need to support the economy while also protecting nature.
support.listeningFocus: Catch the source phrase "According to the lecture" and the paired idea "economic growth with environmental protection".

vocabulary.urban planners: people who design and organize city development
vocabulary.environmental protection: actions that protect the natural world

questions.sentence: The speaker suggested that the decline was gradual rather than the result of a single event.

support.meaning: The speaker believed the decrease happened slowly, not because of one sudden event.
support.listeningFocus: Focus on the contrast structure "gradual rather than" and the ending phrase "a single event".

questions.sentence: Students were expected to infer the author’s attitude from tone, evidence, and word choice.

support.meaning: Students needed to figure out how the author felt by using tone, evidence, and vocabulary.
support.listeningFocus: Listen for the academic verb "infer" and the three-part list at the end of the sentence.

vocabulary.infer: to figure something out from clues
vocabulary.word choice: the specific words an author decides to use

questions.sentence: As the experiment progressed, the researchers revised their hypothesis to match the new data.

support.meaning: While the experiment continued, the researchers changed their idea so it fit the new information.
support.listeningFocus: Catch the time opener "As the experiment progressed" and the verb phrase "revised their hypothesis".

vocabulary.hypothesis: an idea or explanation that can be tested
vocabulary.data: facts or information collected for study
